notes:
Passed on the fake backend with python3 -m mhs.driver check (G1-G9; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, so the loader refuses the R2 hardware backend; nothing ran on an arm and the hardware backend was never imported or run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family/helper is python-object / PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct Driver with native.py. The upstream entry symbol builds SCS (Feetech) frames from parts (0xFF 0xFF, servo ID, length, instruction, parameters, checksum) and its methods take structured arguments and return bool/None; a family command table cannot express that framed protocol. The card's decision is already direct-driver, so no wire syntax was changed. Covered: one read (joint_positions for servos 1-6 in rad, converted from the upstream degrees), cap.motion.joint_position.v1 (move all six with set_multiple_servo_angles, then poll the present positions and report reached), cap.motion.home.v1 (the upstream go_home pose, read back; homed), the safe-state extension x-cap.itheima1.disable_all_torque.v1 (sync_disable_torque on IDs 1-6), @estop (the same native torque-off), @reset (sync_enable_torque), and a driver-side read-back wait bounded by the request deadline. Not covered: cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 (the entry class ServoControllerStandalone has no Cartesian method; the module-level inverse kinematics needs a Windows lookup-table file and is not part of the entry symbol), single-servo commands (set_servo_angle, set_position and read_position are implemented in the fake but not bound separately), motion speed on joint moves (the upstream default speed=0 is the highest speed; only the home action exposes the class's speed_scale, operator_required), the SCS wire protocol and the serial port itself, the sync-read fallback on a real bus, and the hardware path. The fake does not model motion over time, serial framing, or the servo's own range checks; its start positions and torque state are placeholders marked # placeholder. The fake's surface was checked against the clone's AST by G7. Limits: joint_positions is 0..pi rad per joint, cited to sources/servo_control_standalone.py:468-471, where set_servo_angle converts 0-180 degrees to the 1024-3072 position range and clamps there. G4.REF_VALUE is the one remaining warning: the cited line states the bound as 0-180 degrees and the catalogue class fixes the unit to rad, so the driver's upper bound is pi and the line does not show 3.14159; this is the same bound converted, not a second value. The home speed_scale is Limit.operator_required (the catalogue class defines a dimensionless 0..1 fraction and the clone states no speed-scale range for the arm); site-limits.example.json is an example overlay that fills and narrows it to 0.1..0.5, not a device fact. Safety: the clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so SAFE-045 is met by the safe-state action, not by estop_physical_ref. The upstream licence is NOASSERTION/unknown and the card's publish_review is required, so the owner's publication decision is still needed. check-report.json is regenerated by the gate; gate.digest is the digest line the check printed.
